claims: NASA's Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California on April 10, 2026.
NASA's Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission concluded with the splashdown and was a 10-day mission around the moon.
The Artemis II crew returned in the Orion capsule.
Artemis II marks the first crewed deep-space return in over 50 years.
The Artemis II mission goal is to verify the Orion spacecraft and SLS rocket systems for future lunar missions.
A SpaceX Falcon 9 launch was scheduled for late Friday night (April 10, 2026) from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
The SpaceX Falcon 9 launch was separate from the NASA Artemis II mission
